contexts.text: It brought forth wild grapes (). ( = the evils of hatred and revenge. AC 5117:2.) ( = evils which are opposite to the goods of charity; that is, evils of life. AE 375:31.) ( = that with that nation instead of the goods of truth... there were evils of falsity. AE 433:34.) ( = that instead of good there was wickedness iniquum. AE 918:4.)
The concupiscences of the flesh may be compared to scorched and withered grapes, and to wild grapes; but the affections of the spirit, to juicy and delicious grapes...
Faith without Truths is like a vine which bears wild grapes...
The wild vine instead of barley () = falsity instead of truth.

The fathers have eaten a wild grape, and the teeth of the sons are blunted ()... To eat a wild grape = to appropriate the falsity of evil; for a wild grape, which is a bitter and bad grape, = the falsity of evil... (But as) a man is not punished for his hereditary evils, but for his own evils... it is added... every man that eateth the wild grape, his teeth shall be blunted.
What is bitter = the falsification and adulteration of truth and good, the various kinds of which are signified by wild grapes, etc.
